**The document doesn't give either number.** The values appear only in Figure 11 (p. 9), which is included as an image with no data in the text.

What the text does say about the open-domain experiment:

- **Setup:** Contriever, fine-tuned on MS-MARCO, retrieves the top *k* Wikipedia documents for NaturalQuestions-Open queries. The authors measure retriever recall and reader accuracy as *k* changes (p. 9).
- **Overall finding:** Reader performance levels off long before retriever recall does, so the models aren't making effective use of the extra documents (p. 9; also p. 2).
- **20 vs. 50 documents:** Going beyond 20 retrieved documents improves performance only slightly: about 1.5% for GPT-3.5-Turbo and about 1% for Claude-1.3 (p. 9; p. 2). These are gains, not absolute accuracies. The text attributes the 1.5% to "GPT-3.5-Turbo" and doesn't separately name GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) here.

The Appendix G tables (p. 18) report accuracies for GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K), but they cover the controlled multi-document QA task with 10, 20 or 30 documents. They don't apply to the 50-document open-domain setting.
